functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Long fascicles like its neighbor brachioradialis; most radial of the wrist extensors.
functional_compartments.source: Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

motor_endplate_zones.method: cadaveric dissection -- radial-nerve motor branch entry point (motor point) location, not a Sihler's-stain arborization density map
motor_endplate_zones.notes: In all 30 dissected limbs (100%), the nerve branch to ECRL entered the muscle within its proximal third; the branch itself averaged 2.9 +/- 1.0 motor sub-points and 3.2 +/- 1.0 cm in length. Motor point (nerve entry) is typically close to, but not identical with, the point of densest intramuscular arborization -- treat this range as a proximal-third targeting zone rather than a fine-grained endplate band.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Caetano EB, Vieira LA, Sabongi Neto JJ, Caetano MBF, Picin CP, Silva Junior LCN, 'Anatomical Study of the Motor Branches of the Radial Nerve in the Forearm', Rev Bras Ortop (Sao Paulo) 55(6):764-770 (2020), doi:10.1055/s-0040-1713403 (https://doi.org/10.1055/s-0040-1713403) -- 30 limbs from 15 adult cadavers -- retrieved via PubMed

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

trigger_points.location_description: Muscle belly about 3-5 cm distal to the lateral epicondyle, radial to extensor carpi radialis brevis and just dorsal to brachioradialis.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Lateral epicondyle region and the radial dorsal wrist over the anatomical snuffbox and the bases of the 1st-2nd metacarpals; painful weak grip is the characteristic complaint.
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Repetitive gripping with wrist extension (racquet backhand, mouse and keyboard work, scrubbing, hand-shaking), lifting with a pronated forearm; commonly co-exists with brachioradialis, extensor carpi radialis brevis, supinator and extensor digitorum trigger points.
trigger_points.notes: Active ECRL trigger points reproduced the presenting pain in 12 of 20 patients with lateral epicondylalgia (Fernandez-Carnero et al. 2007). Non-myofascial differential: intersection syndrome, De Quervain's disease, radial sensory neuritis, STT and basal-joint arthritis, scaphoid pathology, dorsal wrist ganglion, scapholunate injury, C6 radiculopathy.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons (1999) Trigger Point Manual, 2nd ed., Vol. 1, ch. 34; Donnelly et al. (2019) 3rd ed., ch. 34, pp. 329-342 -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded wrist muscle reference.
